newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee eases vs forward dlr, gains in spot.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee eases vs forward dlr, gains in spot.

text.p: The Indian rupee slipped against the forward dollar but ended up in the spot market on Wednesday, dealers said.
"Call money rates had reached their low with no room to fall further," said a dealer, explaining why premia rose in the forward dollar market.
"The market was heavily received, looking to cut positions."
There was an element of profit-taking which also aided the rise in premia, dealers said. "There is also genuine paying interest around 7.0 percent," said a forward dealer at a foreign bank.
The chief dealer at a state-run bank said a newspaper report about the government's plans to raise over 50 billion rupees from the market also helped push up the premia.
July dollars ended at 1.46/1.49 rupees, up from the opening level of 1.39/1.42 rupees, dealers said.
Towards the close of trading on Wednesday, the finance ministry announced state government loans worth 16 billion rupees on January 20.
The spot rupee closed at 35.87/88, up from the opening level of 35.88/89, dealers said. Moderate corporate dollar demand in the morning session took the rupee to the day's low of 35.90.
Dollar sales at this level pushed the rupee to the 35.87 level, with stray deals at a high of 35.8650, dealers said.
Several dealers said they expected the effective outlflow of about $1.0 billion on redemptions of India Development Bonds beginning next week.

One dealer at a foreign bank said dollar demand from state-run companies were piling up and he expected this demand to hit the market later this week or next week, pushing the rupee to the 35.95/96 level.

A dealer at another foreign bank said keeping the rupee stable is perhaps the only positive step taken at a time when the oil pool defict had risen to a staggering 200 billion rupees from the earlier estimate of 150 billion rupees.
